author: Synthetic Generator
content:
Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) has dropped plans to borrow for Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) chips and will instead raise about $8 billion in new equity, a report said. Analyst Dan Ives says Starlink cash flow is not needed for the purchase.

The equity raise would be led by Goldman Sachs. Apollo Global Management (NYSE:APO) is not expected to take part, and no bank loans or investment-grade debt are planned.

Ives said Apollo has not backed any xAI deals this year. He also said Nvidia does not hold a SpaceX stake, and that the Colossus 2 chip count will stay flat through December.

Ives lowered his rating to Neutral and set a $150 price target. At publication, SPCX was up 1.5% at $170.20, and the $8 billion raise equals about 0.4% of the company's roughly $2.21 trillion market value.
headline: SpaceX Scraps $40 Billion Debt Plan for Equity Raise; Ives Downgrades to Neutral
summary: SpaceX reportedly replaced its $40 billion debt plan with an $8 billion equity raise, and Dan Ives downgraded the stock to Neutral.
